subject: Daily AcreetionOS Update -- September 17, 2026
body:
Daily AcreetionOS Update - September 17, 2026

Welcome to today's AcreetionOS daily update for September 17, 2026. We have a solid lineup of developments, community happenings, and tips to share with you today. Grab your coffee and let's dive in.

This week saw some meaningful commits across our repositories, including an intelligence sync that updated our newsletter, archive, and wiki guides. These behind-the-scenes improvements help keep our documentation accurate and our community informed. Quality work like this is what keeps AcreetionOS running smoothly.

On the development front, we also added a new Private Browsing Myths page to our website, tackling common misconceptions about online privacy. This is a great resource for users who want to understand how truly private their browsing habits really are. We encourage everyone to check it out and share it with friends new to Linux.

Our CI pipeline received important fixes recently, including a correction to the release workflow's block-scalar indentation that had broken validation. We also re-triggered the GitLab mirror to resolve a deploy key issue and ensured that firefox-ublock-origin was added back to the Xlibre build. These small but critical fixes keep our release process reliable and our users secure.

In the broader Arch Linux community, the Shelly 3.1.4 GUI package manager has been making waves with significant improvements to its native package builder. Multiple outlets including 9to5Linux and Linuxiac have covered these enhancements in detail. It is exciting to see tools in the Arch ecosystem continue to evolve and mature for all of us.

On a more serious note, a prominent Arch Linux developer announced their resignation after a remarkable ten-year run with the project. Additionally, over 400 AUR packages were hijacked to deploy infostealer malware and eBPF rootkits. We urge all users to stay vigilant about the packages they install and always verify sources carefully before proceeding.

For those interested in the wider Linux landscape, Fedora 45 beta has introduced notable improvements to the Linux console experience. We also recommend reviewing the latest security updates that were released this past Wednesday. Staying current with security patches is one of the best ways to protect your system from emerging threats.

Speaking of security, our new Private Browsing Myths page ties directly into a key AcreetionOS value: keeping you informed and safe without relying on telemetry or corporate tracking. AcreetionOS is built on the principle that your privacy is your right, not a feature to be sold. We are committed to providing a Linux experience that respects that principle every step of the way.

Thank you for being part of the AcreetionOS community as we continue building a sovereign, user-friendly Linux distribution together. If you have news, tips, or contributions to share, reach out to us on our Discord server or through our GitLab instance. We will see you in tomorrow's update.
